details.name: Conflict 9: src/wave/barrel/BreakingFront.ts, the top of update() (merge of #102)
details.value: #107: a `jumped` set and `leading = jumpReach ? leadingCrests(samples, count, tracksOf, pointsOf, followed, jumped)`. #102: `jetCrests = keptCrests(...)` and `plainOf = jetCrests ? byColumn(previous without the paced points) : pointsOf`. Kept both, #102's first, so the held jets claim their crests before the jump rule looks. leadingCrests now takes `plainOf` instead of `pointsOf` and the `jetCrests` map, and skips `kept?.has(s)`. Why: the sample loop gives a crest to a jet-holding point first, then to a plain point by z, then to a track. Without the exclusion the jump rule can give the same crest to a sized track: the track is marked followed but never advanced, so it is silently dropped and the crest restarts as an unsized track. Padang Padang runs both rules (PADANG_FRONT jumpReach 10, plus the crash). scores.item: 1. The curl reads as a plunging tube: lip throw, thickness, curvature, cavity
scores.evidence: In curl-close-* (all looks and times) the breaking section is a squat hump about 720x130 px (5.5:1) at x 300-1020, y 318-452. The underside of the lip shows only as a 10-40 px bright strip (x 455-790, y 342-382), and the face below drops straight to the trough, so there is no cavity and no lip falling toward the flats. curl-inside-* shows a straight flat plank (x 780-1280, y 0-335) beside open sky. The whitewater sheet's curl-inside row shows a flat teal void. Only ww-shoulder-rich-sunset (x 700-860, y 330-385) hints at a thrown, back-lit lip.
scores.worstDefect: No cavity. The curl reads as an eyelid or folded green tarp, not a round Padang tube (D01, D02, D03).

scores.item: 2. The lip joins the face as one continuous sheet: no detached slab or floating parts
scores.evidence: In curl-behind-rich-sunset (x 595-870, y 315-455) the curl is two separate shell-shaped slabs floating off the main ridge, one with a peach cap at x 605-660, y 338-362. The lip slab in curl-inside-* carries a dark crack seam (x 1080-1280, y 20-115). In the whitewater sheet's curl-inside row, the lip edge is a saturated navy ribbon over a flat teal fill.
scores.worstDefect: Seen from behind, the curl is two detached slabs on the water, not one sheet joined to the crest (D04).

scores.item: 3. The peel and progression along the crest
scores.evidence: The curl is an isolated pod. There is no shoulder tapering ahead of it, and the curl sheet has no broken section behind it. curl-close ends in a vertical-walled pit at x 940-1035, y 375-452. In curl-channel-rich-midday a short hump (x 525-720, y 338-380) sits on a line that is not breaking. In ww-beside the broken part is one straight foam stripe running to the horizon, with no progressive curl down the line.
scores.worstDefect: Nothing peels: one hump stops dead in a trench (D13, D22).

scores.item: 4. Foam where it belongs (behind the curl, on the flat) and a clean face before touchdown
scores.evidence: The curl sheet has no whitewater behind the curl at all. The flats in front of the wave carry a white Voronoi crackle net (curl-close y 380-720) that reads as leftover foam lace on water that should be glassy. In the whitewater sheet the foam is a flat lattice decal that also covers the near foreground in ww-shoulder (x 0-1280, y 365-720) and ends in straight, hard edges.
scores.worstDefect: The foam is a flat giraffe-print decal, and lace-like crackle covers the clean water in front of the wave (D06, D10).

scores.item: 5. Scale and proportion against Padang Padang: wave height, tube size, the reef
scores.evidence: The wave reads knee-to-waist high. From the channel and the front the curl takes up about 1% of the frame. No coral, ledge or draining trough appears anywhere. The Bukit limestone cliffs are replaced by a flat, untextured beige plane with stair-step edges (curl-behind-rich-sunset y 145-240). The lineup shot is an empty sea. The foreground water is olive or grass-green (hue 68-106 degrees, e.g. RGB 138,146,85).
scores.worstDefect: None of the Padang cues are present: no cliffs, no reef, no lineup, and pond-coloured water (D08, D09, D19).

scores.item: 6. Continuity along the front: no splits, double fronts or abrupt ends
scores.evidence: curl-close ends in a cookie-cutter pit at x 940-1035, y 375-452. curl-behind splits into two slabs. In the channel and front shots a hard straight boundary between green and olive water is seamed with about 4,000 px of saturated blue dashes (RGB about 28,77,151) at y 400-580. In ww-behind the foam band starts abruptly at the puffs.
scores.worstDefect: The breaking section terminates in a near-vertical trench wall (D13).

scores.item: 7. Spray and mist at the lip and at the crash
scores.evidence: None of the 17 images shows lip feathering, an offshore plume off the back, spit out of the tube, or mist over the crash. The only particles are soft round discs in ww-shoulder-rich-sunset (x 60-360, y 380-560) and ww-beside (x 300-560, y 180-300).
scores.worstDefect: No spray at all, though offshore spray off the back is Padang's signature (D07).

scores.item: 8. The crash and the foam ball
scores.evidence: The curl sheet has no crash. In the whitewater sheet the 'foam ball' is 2-3 blurry, semi-transparent billboard puffs floating above the water: ww-behind x 595-660, y 322-378; ww-shoulder x 605-710, y 315-362 (grey smoke); ww-beside x 570-690, y 305-375. There is no impact splash, no churning white volume and no droplets, and the whitewater behind them is a flat lattice.
scores.worstDefect: The foam ball reads as two cotton-ball or smoke puffs (D05).

defects.image: look/r1/ww/ww-behind-rich-midday.png, ww-shoulder-rich-sunset.png, ww-beside-rich-midday.png (ww water-sheet rows ww-beside, ww-shoulder, ww-behind, ww-below, curl-close, curl-front)

defects.productionBar: The Padang foam ball is a brilliant, dense, volumetric white mass that fills the back of the tube and blows out as spit, with sharp textured edges, half sunk into the water. Production games build it from layered high-res flipbook particles plus mesh or volume foam, as in the shoreline crashes of Horizon Forbidden West and Uncharted 4 and the storm waves of Sea of Thieves.

defects.image: look/r1/ww/ww-behind-rich-midday.png; ww-shoulder-rich-sunset.png; ww-beside-rich-midday.png; ww water-sheet curl-close row (y 1080-1260)

defects.productionBar: Fresh whitewater after a Padang barrel is a thick, opaque, lumpy volume about a metre high that tumbles and self-shadows. Decaying lace has filaments a few centimetres wide with irregular holes and thins out with time. Compare Sea of Thieves foam, Unreal Water/Crest foam, or any photo.

defects.image: All 17 images (both water sheets and every close-up)
defects.region: The lip line and crash zone in every shot
defects.what: There is no spray anywhere: no feathering off the lip, no offshore plume off the back, no spit from the tube, no mist over the crash.
defects.productionBar: Padang is offshore in the dry-season SE trades, and every set throws a spray plume off the back of the lip; the spit is the signature shot. True Surf and Surf World Series emit continuous spray particles along the lip.

defects.region: Land: curl-behind-rich-sunset x 0-1280, y 145-240 (stair-step edge at x 0-450, y 150-190); ww-behind x 0-1280, y 138-170; curl-inside x 0-735, y 318-355. Flats: curl-channel and curl-front x 0-1280, y 450-720
defects.what: The Padang environment is missing. The land is a flat, unlit beige plane with rectangular stair-step edges, and the reef flats are a featureless olive/khaki plane. There are no limestone cliffs, no vegetation, no coral heads and no reef ledge.
defects.productionBar: Padang Padang is a small cove under steep limestone cliffs with green scrub. Dark brown coral shows through clear turquoise water in the trough, and the ledge drains at low tide. These cues sell both scale and place.

defects.region: Foreground water: channel (640,640) RGB 138,146,85; front (640,600) RGB 136,145,95; close (640,640) RGB 88,127,76
defects.what: The foreground water is olive or grass-green (hue 68-106 degrees) and reads as a pond or pea soup. Only the wave face (hue about 170) is ocean-coloured.
defects.productionBar: Bali reef water is turquoise to cyan (hue about 175-195) over sand, deepening to sapphire-teal on the face, with bright aqua translucency in the lip.

defects.productionBar: In real tubes the cavity is darker than the face and lip, the ceiling glows aqua with light through the lip, and the lip's leading edge is a thin bright line.

defects.what: A hard dark navy/black line runs along the lip slab, with a small dark notch below it. It looks like a mesh crack, an exposed back face or a depth-test seam.

defects.what: A hard-edged orange glyph-like cutout sits on the back of the lip and reads as a decal or a blown-out specular.

surf critic r1.improvedSinceLast: This is the first critic round. r1 is the only round in look/, so there is nothing earlier to compare against. The most promising frame is ww-shoulder-rich-sunset, where the back-lit lip at x 700-860 begins to throw. Every other frame fails the rubric outright.

scores.item: 1. The tube reads instantly from the channel and front views
scores.evidence: In curl-channel-rich-midday the barrel is a 200x45 px hump at (520-720, 338-382). That is 16% of the frame width, sitting on the horizon, while 55% of the frame is a khaki foreground plane. In curl-front-rich-midday it is a 285x47 px lens at (430-715, 335-382). All 12 channel and front cells on the curl sheet read as a swell or a submarine hull, not a tube. Only curl-close shows an overhang, and even there the opening is a slit 10-40 px tall. The lip barely projects, and the section ends in a hard-cut pit at x≈1000-1025.
scores.worstDefect: The tube is a tiny horizon hump with no pitching lip, no visible eye and no peeling wall, so nothing says 'barrel' at a glance.

scores.item: 2. The inside shot delivers the in-the-barrel moment
scores.evidence: In curl-inside-rich-midday, -classic-midday and -rich-sunset, about 60% of the frame is open sky with cumulus. The 'wave' is a straight diagonal slab from (775,335) to (1280,0) topped by a flat white strip. There is no curtain overhead, no exit window, no foam ball, no spit or mist, and the wall is a uniform dark green with no translucency. The whitewater run is worse: in the ww sheet's curl-inside row the sky is replaced by a flat teal fill measured at RGB(54,126,131).
scores.worstDefect: The camera is not inside a tube at all. It sits beside an open planar wall under a wide-open sky.

scores.item: 3. Lighting mood at each time of day
scores.evidence: The skies do differ: a pink dawn gradient, a photographic midday cumulus HDRI and a warm sunset. lineup-rich-sunset also has a passable glitter path. The water barely responds, though: it is the same mint or khaki at every time of day (close water ≈ RGB 98,138,93; khaki ≈ 137,145,93). The rich-dawn barrel interior glows with swimming-pool caustics at (590-1000, 360-445). The sunset sky has a brown smoke-like blob at (730-1280, 100-325), and the sun core is saturated yellow RGB(255,233,67), darker-looking than its halo RGB(255,231,140). ww-shoulder has posterized hard-edged orange patches. All twelve 'below' frames are murky, with mean RGB of about (15,65,65).
scores.worstDefect: The water does not carry the time of day: the same flat green and khaki at dawn, noon and sunset, with no light transmission through the lip except an airbrushed gold patch.

scores.item: 4. Silhouette, depth and atmospheric perspective
scores.evidence: The coastline is a gray-box beige slab with ruler-straight edges: curl-inside at 0-730 x 320-355, ww-behind at 0-1280 x 140-170, and a stepped plateau at 0-1280 x 145-240 in curl-behind-rich-sunset. There are no cliffs, vegetation or reef. The barrel silhouette has no lip thickness, spray or feathering. Classic horizons are a razor-sharp line with a dark navy band and no haze. The edge of the detail or simulation patch shows as a hard trapezoid on the open ocean (sheet horizon row). The Voronoi foam cells stay the same size at every distance, and the underwater shots have no depth gradient.
scores.worstDefect: A gray-box beige slab stands in for Padang Padang's limestone cliffs and jungle, so neither depth nor location reads.

scores.item: 5. Would this frame sit beside a shipped AAA screenshot without embarrassment
scores.evidence: Every frame with a wave shows rendering bugs at 1:1: a single-pixel dot lattice on the barrel face, saturated blue scanline dashes (4231 px below the horizon in the channel frame against 0 in the lineup control), a hard-cut pit, and a flat teal fill in place of the sky. On top of those come the placeholder land, Voronoi 'giraffe' foam and cotton-ball foam sprites. The best frame, lineup-rich-sunset, has no wave in it, and it still shows the smoke blob and the sun-core artifact. On its own it might score 4/10.
scores.worstDefect: Visible render bugs on the hero subject in every hero shot (dot lattice, blue dashes, cut geometry, missing sky).

shot critic r1.improvedSinceLast: This is the first critique round (r1), so there is no earlier round to compare against. These scores are the baseline.

defects.image: r1/curl/curl-inside-rich-midday.png (same in curl-inside-classic-midday.png, curl-inside-rich-sunset.png, and all six curl-inside cells of curl/water-sheet.png at y 900-1080)
defects.region: Full frame. Open sky covers x 0-1280, y 0-330 left of the wall. The wall is a straight diagonal slab from (775,335) to (1280,0), and the lip is a flat white band running from (780,330) to (1280,30).
defects.what: The camera sits beside an open, steep, flat wall rather than inside a tube. Nothing arcs overhead and about 60% of the frame is open sky. There is no ceiling, no curtain falling into the water ahead, no exit window, no foam ball chasing, no spit, mist or lens droplets, and the wall is a uniform dark green with no translucency gradient. The shot fails its whole purpose.
defects.productionBar: GoPro POV barrels at Padang Padang and Pipeline show the lip curtain arcing over the camera and down into the flat water ahead. It frames a bright elliptical window to the channel that fills 25-35% of the frame. The wall glows translucent turquoise near the lip and darkens toward the trough, with spray and mist in the air and droplets on the lens. Surf games (True Surf, Barton Lynch Pro Surfing) and offline CG (Surf's Up, Moana) always enclose the camera.

defects.image: r1/ww/water-sheet.png, curl-inside row (sheet y 1620-1800, all 6 cells)
defects.region: In each cell, x≈130-320 and y≈0-95, which is about frame x 520-1280, y 0-380.
defects.what: With whitewater enabled, the sky is replaced by a solid, untextured teal fill measured at RGB(54,126,131), with a hard horizontal edge at mid-frame. The camera appears to be below the surface with a constant fog colour. The lip is a flat-shaded white wedge at midday and a peach one at sunset, with a saturated navy shard under it.
defects.productionBar: Frames that straddle the waterline use a meniscus split, Snell's window and the real sky above (Subnautica, Sea of Thieves diving). A constant colour fill never ships.

defects.image: r1/curl/curl-channel-rich-midday.png and r1/curl/curl-front-rich-midday.png (and all 12 curl-channel and curl-front cells of curl/water-sheet.png, rows y 180-360 and 540-720)
defects.region: Channel barrel at (520-720, 338-382), about 16% of frame width and 6% of height. Front barrel at (430-715, 335-382).
defects.what: The tube is a tiny dark-green lens or hump with a white stripe on the horizon. The lip never reaches the trough, the tube opening is not visible, there is no wall peeling along the reef, no whitewater behind the section and no offshore spray. It reads as a swell or a submarine hull. The camera framing also centers a dead-level horizon and gives most of the frame to the foreground.
defects.productionBar: Padang Padang channel photos (for example from the Rip Curl Cup contest) make the wave the subject, filling 40-70% of the frame width. They show a long left-hand wall with the lip pitching out in a thick round arc to the flat water, a dark tube eye, spit, offshore spray blowing off the back, and whitewater cascading behind the section.

defects.region: Channel: everything below the diagonal from (0,575) to (1280,365). Front: 0-1280 x 455-720. Inside: 0-700 x 340-395. ww-behind: 0-1280 x 165-390 (olive with a white crackle). Curl-behind sheet cells: the right third.
defects.what: The near-field and shallow water renders as an opaque khaki or olive plane, measured at RGB(137,145,93) in front and (136,144,83) in channel. It reads as a mud flat or a field. There is no transparency, no sky reflection at grazing angles, no caustics and no reef, and absorption is missing, since sand seen through water must shift toward cyan or turquoise. The channel is meant to be deep water and should read deep blue-teal.

defects.region: Whole frame
defects.what: There are no scale cues: no surfer, boards, photographers' boats or crowd in the lineup. As a result the wave reads anywhere from 1 m to 3 m high.

scores.item: 1. Lip and curl translucency: the thin sheet lit from behind
scores.evidence: At midday the lip is an opaque, glossy grey-white strip (median RGB 140,158,160) in curl-close-rich-midday and curl-close-classic-midday at x 450-800, y 335-385. In curl-inside-rich-midday it is a flat pale-blue slab like a windscreen (x 780-1280, y 0-330). Only at sunset and dawn does the top of the lip get a flat gold fill (curl-close-rich-sunset x 600-760, y 330-365, RGB 210,169,79). There is no gradient from the thin edge to the thick base, no transmitted light reaching the face, no feathering spray, and no darker underside. In real Padang photos the thin top edge glows aqua or emerald and white appears only where the water is aerated.
scores.worstDefect: B8: the lip renders as an opaque white plastic or glass strip with hard parallel edges (curl-close-rich-midday x 450-800, y 335-385; curl-inside x 780-1280, y 0-330)

scores.item: 2. Interior and throat: depth, the darkening gradient, the green room
scores.evidence: No shot shows a green room. In curl-inside the camera sits at the base of an open face and the sky fills the upper-left ~40% of the frame, with no ceiling and no oval opening. In the ww sheet's curl-inside row, the place where the lip's underside should be is a uniform teal (median 54,126,131, std about 3). The midday throat is an opaque olive slot (40,96,63) that ends in a hard wall at x≈1020. The dawn throat is lit by a yellow-green swimming-pool caustic web, so it is brighter than the face, which is the reverse of a real tube.
scores.worstDefect: B9: flat teal ceiling with zero detail where the underside of the lip should be (ww/water-sheet.png, curl-inside row, top-right of every tile)

scores.item: 3. Surface micro-detail at close range: normals and ripples, no plastic or smeared look
scores.evidence: The near field in every curl-close frame is large flat facets bounded by sharp white ridges (x 0-1280, y 430-720), with no capillary or multi-octave detail inside the facets. The steep face in curl-inside-rich-sunset shows moiré contour stripes (x 830-1280, y 230-420). The barrel face streaks toward a point (curl-close x 450-1000, y 380-450). The lineup near field (lineup-rich-sunset y 560-720) is a smeared, magnified normal map. The ripple scale on the wave matches the open water, which removes any sense of scale.
scores.worstDefect: B5: a polygon-net highlight pattern with flat facet interiors over half of every curl-close frame

scores.item: 4. Foam and lace: texture, scale and motion cues, no tiling or cellular-pattern artefacts
scores.evidence: Every whitewater shot is uniform Worley/Voronoi cells. ww-shoulder-rich-sunset is a milky translucent sheet punched with hard-edged convex holes 40-180 px wide, like leopard print. ww-behind-rich-midday has the same holes, plus an even thin-line cell network over the whole far field (x 240-1280, y 180-380). ww-beside x 0-560, y 180-650 and the ww curl-close row (all 6 columns) look the same. The foam has no thickness, bubbles, self-shadowing or flow-aligned stretching. The foam-ball sprites are grey, blurry cotton balls that are darker than the foam they sit on. Spray is uniform orange discs. From below, the foam is a flat grey lattice film.
scores.worstDefect: B4: Voronoi 'giraffe' foam with uniform hard-edged holes (ww-shoulder-rich-sunset x 0-1280, y 380-720)

scores.item: 5. Specular, Fresnel and reflections plausible at dawn, midday and sunset
scores.evidence: The one passable element is the sun-glitter path in lineup-rich-sunset. Against that: saturated cobalt dashes appear at grazing angles (curl-channel y 400-575; curl-front y 465-490; curl-close x 1050-1280, y 345-400). The white star glints are not driven by the sun: high-pass correlation of the curl-close foreground is 0.77-0.90 across dawn, midday and sunset. At dawn the glints are cyan-white (158,185,195) under a mauve horizon sky (150,142,143). At sunset the near water stays mint green (72,116,82) where Fresnel at a grazing view should pick up the warm sky. The lip reflects like a mirror slab. The sun disc has a darker core. The classic midday sun path is a milky wash with no individual glints.
scores.worstDefect: B3: cobalt-blue dash artefacts where reflection or refraction samples go wrong at grazing angles (curl-channel-rich-midday x 0-1280, y 400-575)

scores.item: 6. Colour and absorption: water reads as water at each thickness and depth
scores.evidence: The water has almost no blue: foreground (80,120,80) at midday and (62,108,75) at dawn, throat (40,96,63), inside face (19,92,63). B≈R reads as pea or sage green rather than Padang's aqua and teal. The channel and front foregrounds are flat khaki (139,148,88). The land plane is an unlit constant (213,196,151) that is identical at dawn, midday and sunset. Colour does not change with thickness: the lip is not brighter or more cyan than the base. Underwater is near-black teal (5,47,48). At dawn the throat is brighter than the face.
scores.worstDefect: B7: flat khaki region covering ~40% of the channel and front shots (curl-channel-rich-midday and curl-front-rich-midday, y 440-720)

scores.item: 7. Artefacts: seams, hard lines, z-fighting, stretching, aliasing, holes, flat-colour regions
scores.evidence: An unresolved screen-door dither covers up to 12.6% of 16-px blocks (curl-close-rich-sunset), 6.3% in curl-close-rich-dawn and 4.7% in curl-behind-rich-sunset. Other artefacts: black-dot holes on the far waterline; cobalt dashes; a hard mesh cut at the barrel's right end; a vertical crease down the inside face; a dark crease along the lip; a dithered quad with hard edges; an LOD seam with visibly repeating texture at the dawn horizon; moiré; a hard-edged shadow cutout; a faceted silhouette seen from below. Flat-colour regions: tan land, teal tube ceiling, khaki foreground, and an almost featureless underwater view (gradient detail 0.9-1.7 vs 4-16 for surface tiles).
scores.worstDefect: B1: unresolved ordered-dither or alpha-hash dot grid in the band where the barrel meets the ocean (curl-close-rich-sunset y 380-520, full width)

scores.item: 8. Classic as a credible base look, Rich clearly richer
scores.evidence: Classic has every blocker above, so it is not a credible base. Rich differs from classic by only 6-11/255 mean absolute difference at midday. Rich has less gradient detail than classic in 20 of 45 wave-shot tiles (17 of 30 in the ww sheet, e.g. ww-beside midday 17.0 vs 15.8, ww-behind midday 16.0 vs 13.9). Rich adds the cobalt dashes in the dawn channel tile. curl-inside rich midday and classic midday are visually the same frame. The only clear Rich win is sunset lineup and horizon glitter (detail 8.6 vs 3.5).
scores.worstDefect: M16: Rich is not clearly richer and is flatter than Classic in nearly half the wave tiles

defects.region: Band y 380-520 across the full width, plus x 1040-1280, y 370-700 (12.6% of 16-px blocks). Also: curl-close-rich-dawn (6.3%, same band), curl-close-rich-midday and curl-close-classic-midday (lip top x 575-720, y 320-395; right shoulder x 950-1280, y 340-470), curl-behind-rich-sunset (back of the wave x 600-880, y 330-450), curl-front-rich-midday x 585-650, y 390-415, ww-beside x 590-700, y 390-470 and x 900-1100, y 600-700, ww-below x 800-1115, y 10-200. Masks: scratchpad/look/r1review/dmask_*.png
defects.what: A regular single-pixel dot grid (dark green, cream and orange dots) is drawn straight to screen. This is ordered dither, alpha hash or a dithered crossfade with no temporal or spatial resolve. It concentrates where the barrel mesh meets the base ocean and on the whitewater and foam layers, so it is most likely the barrel-to-ocean blend or the foam-sheet transparency.
defects.productionBar: Shipped titles either resolve hashed or dithered alpha with TAA/TSR so no pattern is visible at rest, or use real blended transparency with depth-based soft intersections. No AAA frame shows a Bayer grid on the hero water surface.

defects.region: x 0-740, y 355-400 (the same in curl-inside-classic-midday and curl-inside-rich-sunset). Saturated dark-blue rim along the waterline at x 0-250, y 380-395 and along the face silhouette at x 700-790, y 340-370

defects.region: x 0-1280, y 400-575: a chain of saturated cobalt dashes 1-3 px tall along the khaki/green boundary. Also curl-front-rich-midday x 680-1230, y 465-490; curl-close-rich-midday x 1050-1280, y 345-400 and x 160-500, y 418-424; curl/water-sheet.png curl-channel row, rich columns (dawn shows them only in rich)
defects.what: Isolated saturated blue dashes, as if a reflection or refraction lookup returns raw sky blue past a hard threshold, such as a total-internal-reflection or Snell-window branch, or a screen-space miss with no fallback. The rich path adds them.
defects.productionBar: Grazing-angle reflections in shipped water are smooth: mip-filtered environment sampling, normals flattened with distance, a fallback for screen-space misses. No isolated saturated dashes.

defects.region: x 0-1280, y 380-720. Also ww-behind-rich-midday x 600-1280, y 350-600 (holes) and x 240-1280, y 180-380 (even line network); ww-beside-rich-midday x 0-560, y 180-650; ww/water-sheet.png curl-close row, all 6 columns
defects.what: Whitewater is a translucent milky sheet with uniformly sized, hard-edged convex polygon holes (40-180 px near camera), like leopard or giraffe print. Behind the bore an even Worley line network covers the whole reef flat. The foam has no thickness, bubble texture, self-shadowing or flow-aligned stretching, and the same density everywhere, which reads as tiled.
defects.productionBar: Real Padang whitewater is a thick, bright, aerated mass with turbulent volume near the bore. It decays into irregular stringy lace with widely varying hole sizes, stretched along the current, with clear water between patches. Sea of Thieves, Uncharted 4 and Ghost of Tsushima use advected multi-octave foam textures with breakup and coverage masks; uniform cells never show.

defects.region: x 0-1280, y 430-720. The same in curl-close-rich-dawn, curl-close-rich-sunset, curl-close-classic-midday; curl-behind-rich-sunset x 480-1280, y 420-720; curl/water-sheet.png curl-close and curl-behind rows, all columns
defects.what: White star or shard highlights form a cellular net around flat green facets with no detail inside them. It reads as a swimming-pool caustic texture laid over the sea. The pattern is the same at all three times of day (foreground high-pass correlation 0.77-0.90 for dawn, midday and sunset), so the sun does not drive it.
defects.productionBar: Real sea glints are many small, sharp highlights whose density follows wave-slope statistics and gathers in the sun's glitter path, while sky reflection varies smoothly with Fresnel. AAA oceans (Uncharted 4, Sea of Thieves, MSFS) use multi-cascade FFT or Gerstner normals with no visible cell structure.

defects.region: x 0-1280, y 145-245 (a stepped mesa on the right, y 175-240). Also ww-behind-rich-midday x 0-1280, y 140-175 plus an olive band at y 160-210; curl-inside-* x 0-730, y 320-345; ww-beside x 0-160, y 145-160; curl/water-sheet.png curl-behind row, all columns
defects.what: An untextured beige plane with RGB exactly (213,196,151) at dawn, midday and sunset in both looks, so it is unlit. It has straight edges and a stepped plateau. The ocean meets it at a straight 'infinity pool' edge with no shore foam, swash, wet sand or shore break.
defects.productionBar: Padang Padang's shore is a small sand cove under limestone cliffs and jungle. Shipped games light the land from sun and sky (pink at dawn, gold at sunset) and put a shoreline where water meets land: foam, swash, wet-sand darkening.

defects.region: x 0-1280, y 440-720. curl-front-rich-midday x 0-1280, y 455-720; curl/water-sheet.png curl-channel and curl-front rows, all 6 columns
defects.what: About 40% of the frame is a flat olive-khaki region (median 139,148,88) with almost no surface detail, a hard boundary to the green water, and the B3 dashes along that boundary. Either the camera is under the swell and sees the underside (total internal reflection of the seabed with Snell-window leaks), or refraction shows an untextured seabed with no absorption or reflection. It reads as mud flats, not the channel.
defects.productionBar: The Padang channel is deep blue. Shallow reef seen through clear water shows mottled coral, rock and sand with caustics, and sky reflection takes over toward grazing angles. If the camera dips under the surface, shipped games (Uncharted 4, Subnautica) show a meniscus waterline split, not a flat colour region.

defects.region: Lip band x 450-800, y 335-385 (median 140,158,160); the same in curl-close-classic-midday; curl-front-rich-midday x 430-700, y 335-370; curl-inside-rich-midday and curl-inside-classic-midday x 780-1280, y 0-330
defects.what: The lip is an opaque glossy white or pale-blue strip with hard parallel edges, like plastic or a car windscreen. It has no thickness-dependent transmission, no brightening at the thin edge, no green or aqua glow, no feathering spray, and no darker underside.
defects.productionBar: In real Padang photos at midday the thin top of the lip glows aqua or emerald with transmitted sun and darkens into the thicker curtain. White appears only where the water is aerated: feathering and spit off the lip. Sea of Thieves and Uncharted 4 show this crest translucency at game scale.

defects.region: curl-inside row (sheet y 1620-1800), all 6 columns, top-right ~40% of each tile (tile-local x 130-320, y 0-90). A dark navy or purple knife-shaped sliver runs along the lip in the same tiles
defects.what: Where the underside of the throwing lip (or the sky) should be, there is a uniform teal, median (54,126,131) with std about 3, so zero detail. The lip edge is a dark sliver that looks like a back face or flipped normals.

render critic r1.improvedSinceLast: This is round 1, so there is no earlier round to compare against. The water-sheet PNGs are full colour (377k and 484k unique colours). The banded look when a whole sheet is viewed is from display downscaling, not the renderer, so nobody should chase it. Zoom crops (z01-z26), native-resolution tile strips (s_*) and dither-coverage masks (dmask_*.png) are in <SCRATCH>/look/r1review/ for the engineer.

fixes.cause: barrelMaskGlsl.ts:15-24 picks each pixel of the 1 m seam band between two surfaces with interleaved gradient noise. The file's own source (Jimenez 2014) designed that noise to be averaged over frames, and this renderer has no temporal pass (MSAA only, main.ts:214), so the dot grid shows unresolved. The dots are worst at a low sun because the two halves are shaded differently. The curl draws its share with its own loft normal, richFarNormal, RICH_FAR_FOAM and crestLight off (SweptBarrelMesh.ts:111, 316-318). The water has the crest light, the per-pixel Catmull-Rom normal, flow ripples, churn and plume (WaterSurface.ts:312-316). The result is cream/orange water dots against dark-green curl dots: 12.6 % of 16-px blocks at curl-close-rich-sunset, 6.3 % at dawn. The same grid makes the pale shoulder sheet, the hull outline from behind and curl-inside's specks on the far water (1,443-1,703 isolated dark pixels a frame, uniform in x mod 4). The whole band lies at lift 0: it begins exactly where the rests have brought the lift to 0 (sweptLoft.ts:694-708, 720-727), so the two surfaces coincide there.
fixes.change: (a) The water gives way only where the mask is full: WATER_BARREL_DISCARD becomes mask >= 0.999, with no dither. (b) The opaque curl discards where mask < 0.999. (c) A band mesh carries the band. It is a child of SweptBarrelMesh.mesh and shares the curl's geometry and program, plus a SWEPT_BAND define. It is transparent, with depthWrite off, polygonOffset (factor -1, units -4) and alpha = mask, discarding where mask <= 0 or >= 0.999, so it fades the curl into the water it rests on. It follows setView, sheetShown and facesOut, and SweptBarrel.dispose frees it. With the water cut only at 0.999, the mask's spill past a run's last slice can no longer open holes. That spill comes from node-centred, linearly filtered texels (barrelMaskGlsl.ts:13), and runs end at collapsed or dropped slices (sweptLoft.ts:456-461, 499-503). Keep the export mirrorsBarrelDither, returning true when a fragment reads the mask's cut, so src/scene/waterLooks.test.ts passes unchanged. Classic's snapshots (no barrel) stay byte-identical.
fixes.source: A rendering fix, not a shape. Interleaved gradient noise is meant for temporal accumulation (Jimenez 2014, cited at barrelMaskGlsl.ts:3-6). Blended transparency over coincident geometry is the critics' production bar. The band's placement is sweptLoft's own (REST; LOFT.band 1 m [inferred]). The polygon offset is provisional.
fixes.look: No dot grid anywhere on the water. The curl melts into the sea over its 1 m band at every hour, the shoulder stops reading as a semi-transparent sheet, and the water behind the tube has no dark specks.
fixes.check: Next curl and ww sheets, all three times and both looks: the critics' single-pixel dot mask flags <= 0.5 % of 16-px blocks (was 12.6 % curl-close-rich-sunset, 6.3 % dawn, 4.7 % curl-behind-rich-sunset). Curl-inside has < 50 isolated dark pixels, meaning summed RGB more than 90 below the 4-neighbour mean (was 1,443-1,703). waterSheetCurlLuma's lip, wall and face regions stay within 2 % of today.

fixes.cause: Where the curl rests on the water it is still shaded as the curl. It takes the loft's normal (SweptBarrelMesh.ts:111) with world-xz chop and ripples carrying no current (richFarNormal, :316). Its foam is RICH_FAR_FOAM: no plume, churn, freshness glow or streaks (CLASSIC_FOAM in Classic). Its body is waterBodyFragment(false, ...) (:318), so nothing on the curl gets crest light except the lip's sheet. The water beside it has all of these (WaterSurface.ts:312-316; in Classic, the central-difference normal at :164-175 and the crest light at waterOptics.ts:211-219). That gives the seam its two colours at a low sun, a crease along the inside face (M5, in Classic too) and the hull-on-the-water look from behind. The lifted face and back are not a sheet, so they get no crest light at all: the ruled follow-up 'the curl's crest light at weight 0', whose seam contrast now shows.
fixes.change:
Blend toward the water's own shading by (1 - lift).
- Rich: the normal of richNormalFragment at vWaterWorld.xz (waterCarvedCubic, chop, flow ripples, churn relief). RICH_FOAM, with vWaterFoam and vWaterAir (add richAerationVertexPars) times (1 - lift). The height-field crest light, with the Rich carve replacement as at WaterSurface.ts:312. Include every pars the water's Rich fragment includes, in its order (WaterSurface.ts:309), so groups 2 and 4's changes reach both surfaces.
- Classic: the water's central-difference normal at position.xz in the vertex shader (waterBeginNormal's form), and the same crest-light march.
- Lifted and sheet weight 0: crest light over the profile's own horizontal chord toward the sun. Per vertex, sweptLoft finds the chord through its slice's profile at the vertex's height along +ray and -ray, as a new LoftResult field and attribute. The face and the back are each monotone in height, so one binary search per point. The shader uses chord / max(0.2, |s.ray|), with s the sun's horizontal direction, in the existing CREST_SCATTER form. The sheet keeps its own crest light.
Time the loft with the padangLoft probe and the shot with waterSheetTime.
fixes.source: The water's own model: CREST_SCATTER, waterCrestThickness, and the G8/G9 normal and foam. The advisor's Part B follow-up, assigned now because the seam's contrast shows in the sunset dots. The chord is the Basilisk profile's own geometry.
fixes.look: At dawn and sunset the curl's back and its rests glow like the sea around them. There is no cream-and-green seam and no crease down the face. From behind, the wave is one hump with a backlit crest, not a hull lying on the water.
fixes.check: Draw the band opaque with a dev flag. The curl's band pixels then match the water's within 3/255 at all three times, in both looks. The M5 crease (curl-inside x 725-775, y 450-720) is at most 2 luminance levels. curl-behind-rich-sunset shows no outline along the curl's back.

fixes.cause: The curl's Rich normal, richFarNormal (richWaterGlsl.ts:116-125), samples the ripple tiles (4 m and 1.3 m) and the chop at world xz and adds the slopes in world space. On a near-vertical or overturned surface the xz projection collapses along the profile. The pattern smears into contour stripes on the face (M4: curl-inside-rich-sunset x 830-1280, y 230-410) and streaks toward a point in the throat (curl-close x 450-1000, y 380-450). The curl's residual lace, drawn at world xz by CLASSIC_FOAM and RICH_FOAM, stretches the same way: the ruled follow-up 'residual lace on the curl's lifted face'.
fixes.change: Give each vertex the loft's own surface coordinates as a new attribute: sigma along the crest (sliceSigma) and s, the arc length along the profile from the crest landmark. Build a tangent frame: T is the front's tangent from sweptRay, B = n x T. Where lifted, sample the ripple map and the lace at (sigma, s) and perturb the normal by -(s_x T + s_z B). Blend back to the world-xz mapping as lift goes to 0 (smoothstep 0.1-0.4), so the band stays the water's. No current in the wave's frame [provisional]. In Classic, map the residual lace the same way, and on the curl fade the chop by the world normal's height (smoothstep 0.3-0.7) instead of projecting it. Write this in the curl's own normal chunk; waterChop.ts is Classic's and stays untouched.
fixes.source: The ruled Part B follow-up (a face-aligned foam mapping), extended to the ripples, because a planar xz projection is degenerate on a vertical face [rendering geometry; constants provisional].
fixes.look: The face, throat and underside carry the same fine ripple texture as the sea, running with the wave. No corrugated stripes, and no streaks converging into the tube. Any lace on the rests lies flat on them.
fixes.check: On curl-inside-rich-sunset's face region, the luminance autocorrelation along the profile has no secondary peak above 0.5; today's stripes produce one. On curl-close-rich-midday's throat, no streaks converge. The face's ripple gradient detail is within 0.7-1.3x that of the sea beside it.

fixes.cause:
Three on/off switches with no gradient between them.
(a) The curl's body lights the bed seen through the back wall with the caustic map (caustics on at SweptBarrelMesh.ts:318; waterOptics.ts:203-205), and no lip shadows that map. At dawn the throat (76,122,76) comes out brighter than the face.
(b) RICH_THROAT tests the sun per pixel against the slice's tip and dims it by the lip's mean thickness (SweptBarrelMesh.ts:237-242), so the lip's shadow on the face is a hard, stair-stepped cut-out (M3).
(c) The throat's darkening uses the 2D view factor in the slice's plane and the per-slice 'formed' flag (sweptLoft.ts:633, 714-718). It stops dead at the last formed slice: the hard curved wall where the tube ends (curl-close x 990-1030), and part of M5.
fixes.change:
(a) Both looks, in the sheet hook: where the inner face's sun doesn't leave the tube (sweptLeaves), take bedLight = 1 in the column body, with no caustic focus, before the slant transmission.
(b) Rich: the sun's path through the lip where its own ray crosses it. Interpolate the thickness from the tip, where the sheet's thickness goes to 0, to the root, by where the sun's direction falls between the tip and the crest in the slice plane. This replaces the binary test and the mean, so the shadow fades through the thin edge.
(c) Rich: add the mouth's share of the sky along the crest to the opening's: F_w' = F_w + (1 - F_w - F_l) * 0.5 * (1 - d / sqrt(d^2 + R^2)). Here d is the slice's distance to the mouth (sliceMouth, vSweptTube.w) and R is half the tip-to-throat distance. Ease the throat's weight in over the last slice spacing before the mouth.
fixes.source: The advisor's 2026-10-01 rulings: the sun shadowed under the lip, and the dark throat with a mirrored mouth. graphics.md item 3: dark inside, bright mouth; caustics on a near-vertical moving wall are faint. The point-to-disk view factor and the crossing interpolation are provisional.
fixes.look: A dark green throat that brightens smoothly toward the mouth. No swimming-pool web inside the tube at dawn, a lip shadow that softens where the lip thins, and no wall where the tube ends.
fixes.check: curl-close-rich-dawn: the throat's mean luminance is at most 0.8x the face's (today it is brighter). curl-close-rich-midday: moving along the throat toward the mouth, no step above 3 % between neighbouring 8-px columns. curl-inside-rich-sunset: the shadow edge (x 885-1280, y 410-540) is at least 6 px wide.

fixes.cause:
Three causes.
- The light behind the lip crosses it on the unscattered beam path e^{-c t} (SweptBarrelMesh.ts:146, 162-163), with c = 0.17-0.50 /m at Padang. So 0.1-0.5 m of lip passes 86-98 % of every colour: a white-blue strip with no gradient from the thin edge to the base, and from inside, a windscreen. The glow's lengthened path (k = 8, :206-209) applies only to the direct sun.
- Mirrored rays off the underside point downward and read the lower half of the photo sky: a dimmed mirror of the sky, measured at (65,75,102) three-quarters of the way down kloofendal's panorama. That is the strip's glossy grey.
- Perturbed normals at the fold face away from the eye and fall to R-infinity (waterOptics.ts:226-227). These are the navy creases on the lip, and the knife-shaped sliver seen from below.
fixes.change:
Rich:
- (a) Pass the sheet's diffuse back light (sky and wall) through e^{-a k t}, with the pure-water a (WATER_ABSORPTION) and k = 8, as the glow does.
- (b) Where reflect(-v, n) points below the horizon, the curl's specular IBL takes the sea's own upwelling radiance (R-infinity x the IBL irradiance / pi) instead of the environment's lower half.
- (c) The lip's leading edge whitens where it frays (the ruled follow-up 'with the spray look'), on open slices only. Over roughly the last 0.15 of the lip from the tip, whiteness = 1 - e^{-tau}, with tau = 1.5 W / r (spray-and-mist.md): W is the sheet's thickness there, broken into r = 1 mm drops over a fraying share. Provisional; white only above tau ~ 15.
Both looks:
- (d) A normal guard on the curl: if n.v < 0.05 in view space, n += (0.05 - n.v) v, then renormalise. This is the same formula group 2 applies to the water.
The per-spot absorption terms (group 2) join the lip's path after both groups merge.
fixes.source: graphics.md item 1: exp(-sigma k d) with k ~ 5-20, from Pope & Fry 1997; the advisor's 2026-10-01 start of k = 8. spray-and-mist.md: optical depth, white only above ~15 (decided 2026-09-29 as recommended). Surf's Up course notes: lip trains and a fraying white leading edge. The normal guard is a rendering fix; its constant is provisional.
fixes.look: The lip glows aqua at its thin edge and deepens to green-blue toward its root. From inside the tube it reads as backlit glass with ripples, framing the mouth. It is white only on the fraying tip, with no navy creases or slivers.
fixes.check: curl-close-rich-midday lip band: luminance falls at least 1.3x from tip to root; the mean hue is 160-200 degrees; R/G is at most 0.8x the incident light's. curl-inside-rich-midday underside (x 780-1280, y 0-330): mean saturation at least 0.2 (today it is pale grey-white). No pixel on the curl has B > 1.5 G and B > 2 R.

fixes.cause: [inferred] The level-12 Basilisk undersides carry cell-scale wiggles where they stand near vertical (the ruled follow-up's 'the library's underside wiggles'). The loft's normals fold there; 58 twisted cells were counted at the fold on 2026-10-01. So a low sun glints off a few pixels as a sharp glyph (curl-close-rich-dawn x 700-730, y 352-368), and dark creases cut the lip (curl-inside x 1080-1280, y 20-115).
fixes.change: In the converter (scripts/barrel-library.ts, beside refitTip in src/wave/barrel/caseFromLibrary.ts), run one or two passes of a 1-2-1 filter over the underside points, from the lip tip to the throat, whose tangent is within about 20 degrees of vertical. Keep the tip, throat and crest landmarks fixed, and never let a point cross the upper surface. Re-encode the committed cases on the --keep path: public/barrels/*.bin, barrelLibraryIndex.ts and docs/research/barrel-cases.md. Drawn and collided shapes change alike (one water).
fixes.source: The ruled Part B follow-up. The filter reaches no further than one level-12 cell, so it removes grid noise, not shape [provisional].
fixes.look: The underside's highlight runs as one soft streak along the lip, with no notches, glyphs or creases.
fixes.check: On every case's open frames, the normal turns less than 15 degrees between neighbouring underside points. The held-frames test, the tip fit and the contact tests pass, with the tip's speed within 1 % of today. curl-close-rich-dawn has no orange glyph.

fixes.cause: When the shading normal faces away from the eye, waterBodyFragment drops to R-infinity (waterOptics.ts:226-227). For Padang's clear water that is navy-cobalt (hue 228 degrees). The Rich normal adds chop, ripples and churn per pixel (WaterSurface.ts:313; richWaterGlsl.ts:139-147), and nothing keeps it facing the viewer at grazing angles. So dashes appear exactly where the view grazes: along the edge of the drawn trough (curl-channel y 400-575, curl-front y 465-490), along the far waterline, and on the face's silhouette (curl-inside). The Rich path adds more of them because its normal is busier.
fixes.change: In the Rich water and the far field, add a normal guard right after the normal chunk (WaterSurface.ts:313; FarFieldOcean.ts:167): if n.v < 0.05 in view space, n += (0.05 - n.v) v, then renormalise. The curl applies the same formula (group 1). Classic's programs stay untouched. Put new tests in richOptics.test.ts, and keep the strings src/scene/waterLooks.test.ts asserts (that file belongs to group 4), for example 'richRoughness( roughnessFactor, waterRippleVariance )'.
fixes.source: A rendering fix: a perturbed shading normal facing away from the eye has no physical meaning [constant provisional].
fixes.look: Water at grazing angles keeps its colour and the sky's sheen. No saturated blue dashes along the trough or the waterline.
fixes.check: Pixels with B > 150, B > 1.6 G and B > 3 R in curl-channel, curl-front and curl-close (Rich, all three times): 0. The Classic parity snapshots stay unchanged.

fixes.cause: waterBodyReflectance lengthens the bed's path by the view and sun cosines against the surface normal (waterOptics.ts:153-156, 160-162). Maritorena's 2KH form assumes the bed lies parallel to the surface. On a steep face that puts the bed 'behind' the face at the column's depth, so faces and the throat show Padang's coral (albedo 0.08, 0.08, 0.025, olive): the pea-green (80,120,80; 40,96,63; 19,92,63).
fixes.change: Add a Rich option to waterBodyFragment, off by default so Classic's shader text is unchanged: path = depth x (1/|r_v.y| + 1/|r_s.y|), where r_v = refract(-v, n, 1/1.333) and r_s is the sun's refracted direction, both taken by their world-vertical components. This is the ray the caustic lookup already follows (waterOptics.ts:203-204), and it gives identical results on flat water. Integration once groups 1 and 2 have both merged: SweptBarrelMesh's Rich program passes the same option (one argument), so the curl's back wall and band keep matching the water. Until then, group 1's blended band keeps any mismatch soft.
fixes.source: Maritorena, Morel & Gentili 1994 (the code's own model) and Snell's law, applied with the bed horizontal.
fixes.look: Steep faces take the water's own colour and the light through the crest instead of the reef's olive. The flat sea is unchanged.
fixes.check: On the water's steep faces (ww-beside, and the shoulder in curl-close; Rich, midday), B/R is at least 1.5 (today about 1). The lineup tile's flat sea stays within 2/255 of today. After the integration line, the same check holds on the curl's back wall (curl-inside x 900-1200, y 450-650).

fixes.cause: SPOT_OPTICS.padang (waterOptics.ts:42) carries only grey particles, so R-infinity is blue (228 degrees). The sourced terms off Padang (chlorophyll 0.77 mg/m3, a_g(440) 0.052 /m) were decided for Rich above water too, replacing the grey absorption (underwater-colour.md decisions 5 and 6). Group 3's underwater build brings the 'later' of that decision forward to now.
fixes.source: underwater-colour.md (decided 2026-09-29; used as provisional). Bricaud, Ciotti & Gentili 2012; Bricaud et al. 1998; Mobley's Eq. 1; NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll.
fixes.look: Padang's water turns cyan-teal (about 186 degrees) wherever it is deep enough to show its own colour. The Reef stays blue.
fixes.check: Padang's deep-water hue is 180-195 degrees. The Reef's hue moves at most 4 degrees. Classic is unchanged.

fixes.cause: RICH_SPECULAR (specular.ts:27-28) widens the specular lobe only for the ripple map's unresolved variance. The Catmull-Rom normal, the analytic chop, the churn relief and the loft's interpolated normals add curvature the pixel doesn't resolve. At roughness 0.08 (GGX alpha 0.0064) the sun's glint therefore lands on single pixels along cell and triangle edges: long straight scratches, paper shards, orange shards in foam holes, and the dawn glyph on the lip.
fixes.change: Before richRoughness, add the shading normal's screen-space variance to the slope variance: variance += kappa (|dFdx(n)|^2 + |dFdy(n)|^2), with kappa 0.25-0.5 and the clamp unchanged (MAX_ROUGHNESS 0.6). Add it as a separate line before the existing call, so the asserted call stays. It reaches the curl and the far field through RICH_FOAM and RICH_FAR_FOAM.
fixes.source: The file's own Toksvig/LEAN form, extended to the normal's derivatives [kappa provisional].
fixes.look: Glints become small rounded sparkles that cluster on wave slopes and twinkle, with no slivers or shards. A low sun draws a soft streak along the lip.
fixes.check: In ww-beside and curl-inside, bright components (luminance above 0.9 of the frame's maximum) with aspect above 6 and length above 20 px: 0. lineup-rich-sunset keeps at least 80 % of today's sparkle count in its glitter path.

fixes.cause: rippleTexture.ts:8 defines two ripple tiles, 4 m and 1.3 m, at 256 texels each. At 1-3 m from the camera, each 1.6 cm texel of the 4 m layer is magnified to about 10 px, and nothing shorter than about 5 cm exists. So the near water looks like a smeared, magnified normal map (lineup y 560-720), with no fine detail inside the near field.
fixes.change: Add a third layer on a ~0.35 m tile with |n| 7-28 (wavelengths 1.25-5 cm). Use the same |n|^-2 slope spectrum and rms rule, at weight ~0.35, and add its variance to the LEAN term so it turns into roughness with distance.
fixes.source: Capillary-gravity dispersion: the phase speed is lowest at lambda = 2 pi sqrt(sigma/(rho g)) = 1.7 cm (computed with sigma 0.073 N/m). The amplitude is provisional, as RIPPLE_RMS_SLOPE is.
fixes.look: Crisp fine ripples near the camera that give the wave its scale. Nothing changes far away.
fixes.check: In the near fields (lineup y 560-720, curl-close y 500-720), Rich's gradient detail is at least Classic's and at least 1.3x today's Rich. No new moire appears at 10-40 m.

fixes.cause: [inferred] Rich's dawn horizon tile has an extra boundary at tile y ~ 105. It matches the dense patch's far edge: the 96 m patch is centred 28.8 m ahead of the camera (richPatch.ts:5-6, 51-52), so its edge lies about 77 m out, which lands near tile y 110 from the horizon shot's 14 m eye. Separately, the far field shades without crest light (FarFieldOcean.ts:113) where the tank has it.
fixes.change: First outline the patch and grid rectangles in the horizon shot to find which edge it is. Then blend the terms that differ across it. At the patch's rim, evaluate the vertex-interpolated foam, air and depth per pixel, or blend them over the rim's outer 4 m. At the tank's edge, fade the tank's crest light and per-pixel detail to the far field's over the last ~20 m [provisional].
fixes.source: A rendering-continuity fix; no physics changes [provisional].
fixes.look: An unbroken sea to the horizon at dawn, with no band across it.
fixes.check: Rich horizon tiles at all three times: no row-to-row luminance step above 2/255 across the tile.

fixes.cause: Seen from below, the Rich water uses the above-water formula with a flipped normal; RICH_SPECULAR gives back faces Classic's roughness (specular.ts:27-28). The result is a pale matte ceiling with the foam lattice painted on, and no window or mirror (ww-below).
fixes.change: Build underwater item 2 in Rich only, as decided and prototyped (notes/round5-underwater/prototype-1-2.md and its diff). For faceDirection < 0, refract the view ray out of the water (n = 1/1.333). Inside the 48.6-degree critical angle, show the sky from the environment times (1 - F). Beyond it, total internal reflection mirrors the water's own fogged colour and the bed. Foam and plume glow as a ceiling lit from above, and there are no caustics under whitewater. Fog stays inside the material; group 3 sets it.
fixes.source: underwater.md items 1-2 (decided 2026-09-29, 'now'). Lynch 2014 (the 97-degree window). The prototype measured 97.5-98.4 degrees.
fixes.look: From under the water, a bright rippling disc of sky set in a silver ceiling, with the whitewater glowing overhead.
fixes.check: In ww-below and the below rows (Rich): the window is 95-100 degrees across on flat water, and looking up is at least 4x brighter than looking level (the prototype measured 6.5x). Classic is pixel-identical.

fixes.cause: The camera's underwater test compares the camera's height with the solver's water height. The water sheet's renderView does it at main.ts:305, and PhysicalMode.ts:735-739 (cameraBelowSurface) does it for the game camera, the fog and the sound's muffle (main.ts:575, 926, 940). Under a swept lip, that height is the hump the tube is cut from, so a camera inside the drawn tube counts as underwater. The scene then switches to FogExp2 and a #367e83 background (main.ts:166-167, 1065-1071). That is exactly the critics' flat teal (54,126,131, standard deviation about 3) in every ww curl-inside tile. A chase or tube camera on a barrel ride would do the same.
fixes.change: Use one test, in a new src/game/drawnWater.ts, at both call sites. At a swept spot, count the drawn loft's crossings above the camera on the vertical through it: the same triangles rasterizeBarrelMask walks, or a SweptContact over the drawn loft (sweptContact.ts:199). An odd count means in water, an even count means in air. Where the loft doesn't cover the camera, keep today's solver-height test. Read only LoftResult's positions, indices and indexCount from PhysicalMode's barrelLoft.
fixes.source: The owner's one-water rule: the camera is in whatever is drawn at its position.
fixes.look: Inside the barrel, the mouth shows the sky and the tube keeps its own light. No teal fog, and the sound isn't muffled.
fixes.check: In the ww and curl sheets' curl-inside tiles, no pixel within 3 of (54,126,131) in the top-right 40 %. On a recorded barrel ride at Padang, the underwater flag never sets while the camera is in the drawn cavity.

fixes.cause: SpotSeabed draws an unlit MeshBasicMaterial with painted vertex colours, sand #d6c69c to #2f5f66 by depth (SpotSeabed.ts:12-16, 70). So the land above datum is the same beige at dawn, midday and sunset (the critics' (213,196,151)), and the bed under water ignores the light.
fixes.change: Rich only: switch to a lit material (MeshStandardMaterial, roughness 1, metalness 0) taking the sun light and the photo sky's environment. Under water, use the spot's bed albedo (SPOT_OPTICS; Padang's coral); above datum, use the painted sand as the dry albedo [provisional]. Keep the sun's attenuation and caustics through the water as useCaustics does today. Call SpotSeabed.setLook from main.ts's water-look switch. Classic is unchanged.
fixes.source: underwater.md item 1 (decided: 'a seabed lit by the actual sun'). The prototype measured the bed 43 % darker at dusk.
fixes.look: The land and the reef take the hour's light, pink at dawn and gold at sunset. The bed under water is lit from above and darkens with depth.
fixes.check: The land's mean colour differs between dawn, midday and sunset by at least 20/255 in some channel (today it is identical). Classic is pixel-identical.

fixes.cause: One teal FogExp2 covers every spot and hour (main.ts:166: #367e83, density 0.035). It still shows 61 % contrast at 20 m and fades no colour faster than another: the flat teal band and the near-featureless below row.
fixes.change: Build underwater item 1 in Rich only, as decided. Fog comes from the spot's own optics inside the materials, as per-channel Beer-Lambert with red fading first, in the prototype's form. Apply the 7 m readability floor where the water is murkier, and the decided underwater exposure gain. Below water, the background is the fog's colour at infinite distance. Use waterOptics.ts's deepReflectance and beamAttenuation now; group 2's sourced colour terms take over once both groups merge. Classic is unchanged.
fixes.source: underwater.md and underwater-prototype.md (decided 2026-09-29). underwater-colour.md gives Padang's sighting distance as 18-20 m.
fixes.look: Under water, Padang fades blue-teal with distance, red first, and the bed reads to about 20 m.
fixes.check: At Padang, a black target falls to 2 % contrast at 18-20 m (the prototype's method). Classic is pixel-identical.

fixes.cause: RICH_FOAM paints foam as an opaque mint colour over the water (richWaterGlsl.ts:86-87; waterFoamColor #d8f2e9 at WaterSurface.ts:270), while Rich's 4x gain sits on the body alone (:86). So foam is no brighter than the water it covers (0.92x at the Reef, per foam-and-whitewater.md), and the shoulder's whitewater reads as a milky translucent sheet. The mint tint also ignores the light: the lace comes out cyan-white (157,184,193) under a mauve dawn sky.
fixes.change: In RICH_FOAM and RICH_FAR_FOAM, draw foam as a layer that adds light: R = R_f + T_f^2 R_w / (1 - R_f R_w). Here R_f = cover x R_foam(age), spectrally flat, going from 0.55 for fresh foam to 0.25 for lace and 0.10 for streaks, and T_f = 1 - R_f. Apply Rich's gain to this composite, not to the body alone, which is the decision's intent; whether it should move to the renderer's exposure is owner question 2. The plume's whitening stays underneath, as now. Don't change the text of richNormalFragment, richFarNormal or RICH_REFLECTION; groups 1 and 2 build on them. This group owns src/scene/waterLooks.test.ts: update its Rich foam assertions, and keep its Classic snapshots unchanged.
fixes.source: Koepke 1984 (foam reflectance flat near 55 %, about 41 % averaged over its first second and 16 % over ten), via foam-and-whitewater.md item 1. Decided 2026-09-29.
fixes.look: Fresh whitewater flashes bright white against darker water and fades to dimmer lace. Foam takes the sky's colour, gold at sunset and rose at dawn, instead of mint.
fixes.check: On ww-shoulder and ww-beside (Rich), foam is at least 2x the water's luminance in fresh foam and at least 1.1x in lace. At sunset the foam's R is at least its B. Classic is unchanged.

fixes.cause: foamPattern.ts draws one Voronoi network: 0.7 m cells with one jittered point each (:17-18), cut at a fixed 0.04-cell edge (:28, :217) at every age and distance. At low foam only the cell walls remain. That is the white net around flat green facets over half of every curl-close frame: mint (199,222,215) at midday, in the same place at every hour, so foam rather than glints, and the same net appears in Classic. It also leaves isolated shards. At high foam the cells become uniform convex holes 0.4-0.55 m across: the leopard print on ww-shoulder.
fixes.change:
Rich only; Classic's foamPatternPars stays untouched.
- Bake once at load a tileable foam field of floating particles advected on a compressible random surface flow (compressibility 0.49). The flow gathers the particles into lines and opens holes of widely varying size.
- Keep two stages of its cycle: early (dense with holes) and late (lace and threads).
- Store them in the churn map's free channels: churnTexture.ts goes from RG8 to RGBA8, 1024^2, mipmapped, with churn keeping R and G. No new uniform is needed; only WaterSurface.ts binds them.
- Sample both flow phases and blend them before thresholding, at ~12 m and ~3 m scales.
- Pick the stage by an age proxy: the existing freshness from the void fraction, and the foam value [provisional].
- Make the edge's softness proportional to the pixel footprint.
- Streaks keep the flow's stretch (streaks.ts).
Define this inside waterChurnPars, so the water and the curl (which includes the water's pars, group 1) both get it.
fixes.source: foam-and-whitewater.md item 2 (decided 2026-09-29): Larkin et al. 2009 (surface compressibility 0.49 +/- 0.02); Heitz & Neyret 2018 (blend before thresholding); Kluyskens 2007 (Surf's Up's baked foam life cycle).
fixes.look: Thick white whitewater near the bore breaks into irregular, stringy lace stretched along the current, with clear water between patches. No cells, no net, no visible repeat.
fixes.check: On ww-shoulder-rich-sunset and ww-behind-rich-midday, the holes' areas have a coefficient of variation of at least 1 (uniform cells give about 0.3). The foam mask's autocorrelation stays below 0.3 at every lag from 3 to 20 m. On curl-close-rich, the near field's brightest 1.5 % of pixels no longer form a connected network across the frame.

fixes.cause: RICH_WATER.reflection = 0.5 (richWaterGlsl.ts:97, applied at :104-107) halves the sky the Rich water mirrors, while the body carries 4x. At a low sun the near water stays mint (72,116,82) instead of taking the warm sky. The drawn trough's khaki never turns to sky at grazing angles (curl-channel and curl-front, y 440-720), and the channel reads green rather than blue.
fixes.change: Set it to 1.0: plain Fresnel (n = 1.333, F0 0.020), so the mirrored sky never exceeds the sky it mirrors. The body gain stays until the owner rules on exposure (owner question 2). The waterLooks assertion reads the constant, so it still holds.
fixes.source: Fresnel for water (waterOptics.ts:11-13). The 0.5 was tuned by eye on the water sheet (G8).
fixes.look: Water at grazing angles mirrors the sky: gold and rose at sunset and dawn, blue over the channel. Near water still shows its body colour.
fixes.check: On curl-close-rich-sunset's near water, R/G rises by at least 15 %. Far water is never brighter than the horizon sky above it. The khaki share of curl-channel's lower half falls by at least 30 %.

fixes.cause: richSpray.ts:56-62 lights the foam ball with a constant 0.45 plus 0.6 x the sun on its lit side. That is below the light the water's own foam receives (about 0.75 at midday: albedo ~0.8 under the photo sky's 3.2 x (0.4 + 0.6 sqrt(sin h)) / pi, PhotoSky.ts:66-87). The 0.45 also ignores the sky's colour, and the opacity mix(0.55, 1, churn) and the rim fade make the ball translucent. The 13 balls come out grey, darker than the foam under them, and never warm.
fixes.change: Light the ball as fresh foam: R_foam 0.55 x (E_sky/pi + E_sun max(0, n.L)/pi). Recover E_sky in SprayPoints.setSun from what it already receives: E_sky = REFERENCE_LIGHT x (0.4 + 0.6 sqrt(sin h)) - lum(E_sun) sin h, which is skyExposure's own identity [the sky's colour taken as neutral, provisional]. Add a forward rim when backlit (drops' g ~ 0.86), and apply the same gain the water's foam composite carries (RICH_WATER.bodyGain today). waterLooks.test.ts asserts strings in the spray shaders: keep 'texture( waterChurnMap', '( 1.0 - smoothstep( 0.55, 1.0, r ) )' and 'if ( abs( vKind - 2.0 ) < 0.5 ) {', or list the edit for the merge.
fixes.source: Koepke 1984; spray-and-mist.md drop optics (decided 2026-09-29); PhotoSky.ts:73-87.
fixes.look: Foam balls are bright white at midday and gold-rimmed at sunset, matching the whitewater they tumble on.
fixes.check: On ww-beside, ww-shoulder and ww-behind, the balls' mean luminance is at least that of the foam beneath them (today it is lower). At sunset their rim pixels have R > B.

fixes.cause: richSpray.ts:64-72 draws mist as uniform round discs, lit by Henyey-Greenstein with g = 0.6 (mist.ts:4; water drops are 0.86-0.88) and tinted by the sun's colour. At sunset they become round orange discs that read as bokeh or insects, and the wave has no spray to give it scale.
fixes.source: spray-and-mist.md item 1 (decided 2026-09-29): Bohren 1987; Erinin et al. 2023.
fixes.look: A white core thinning into a glowing veil, and fine streaks with glints. No discs.
fixes.check: ww-shoulder-rich-sunset has no round, uniformly filled sprites larger than 6 px, and mist pixels' saturation stays below 0.35.

fixes.cause: Feathering starts on the absolute offshore wind above 4 m/s (SprayCloud.ts:99, 424-426). At Padang's 3.6-6.7 m/s offshore (Denpasar records), the veil barely exists, and from behind the wave has no spit or spray blowing off its crest.
fixes.change: Start the veil on the wind relative to the crest: the offshore wind plus the crest's speed sqrt(g(h + eta)), with onset at 7-11 m/s. Use drops of ~0.1 mm, launched seaward and upward off the crest's top (off the swept lip's crest where it is drawn), within the decided 16k pool.
fixes.source: spray-and-mist.md item 4 (decided 2026-09-29): Veron 2015; Troitskaya et al. 2017. Wind from the Padang build sheet.
fixes.look: Padang's offshore trades blow a fine veil back off every lip, backlit gold at sunset.
fixes.check: On Padang Medium with its sourced wind, veil particles come off at least 50 % of open slices, and none where the relative wind is under 7 m/s.

rejected.reason: Classic's water outside the barrel has the same R-infinity fallback (waterOptics.ts:226-227). The owner's rule keeps Classic byte-identical, so a bug-only fix there is the owner's call (question 1). Group 2 fixes Rich, and group 1 fixes the curl in both looks.
The white net is Classic's own foam lace (foamPattern.ts, shared by both looks). Group 4 replaces it in Rich only; changing Classic needs the owner (question 1).
Classic's colour is frozen by rule. The bed path and the sourced colour go to Rich (group 2).

rejected.defect: M13 (Classic dawn tile: repeating chop texture and the tank/far-field step)
rejected.reason: Classic's horizon is unchanged by rule. Group 2 handles Rich's boundary.
Classic's milky sun path comes from Classic's roughness (0.62), part of its frozen look. Rich's glitter path is the element the critics passed.

rejected.defect: B4 (part: whitewater thickness, bubbles and self-shadowing)
rejected.reason: Volume means the roller with body (decided 2026-09-29): geometry the rider hits, built on the loft (roller-build.md). That is the owner's next phase, after the face and tube. This round fixes the foam's light and texture (group 4).

rejected.defect: B6 (part: limestone cliffs, jungle and the sand cove)
rejected.reason: Scenery, not water (owner question 4). Group 3 lights the land plane in Rich so it follows the time of day.

rejected.defect: B6 (part: shore break, swash and wet sand at the waterline)
rejected.reason: A swash zone is in none of the owner's decisions; it belongs with whitewater with volume.

rejected.defect: B7 (part: a mottled reef of coral, rock and sand under the shallows)
rejected.reason: The khaki is the coral bed (sourced at 8 %, Hochberg & Atkinson 2003) under the forward rest's few decimetres of water. That water depth is the library's own Basilisk trough over Padang's ~1 m reef flat, so it is physically plausible. A sourced bed texture needs a download (owner question 3). Groups 2 and 4 fix its optics: the grazing guard, and the sky reflection at Fresnel.

rejected.defect: B9 (part: no oval opening or ceiling in the curl sheet's curl-inside)
rejected.reason: The sheet holds on the practice swell's curl, open over at least 3 m of crest (waterSheet.ts:110). A tube that short can't frame a camera at half its height looking 8 m along the crest. Re-shoot the tube rows on &swell=big as well. The teal ceiling itself is fixed in group 3.

rejected.defect: B10 (part: bubble-plume volume, light shafts, drifting specks, sand clouds, the tube's cavity from below)
rejected.reason: These are underwater items 3-8, which come after items 1-2 in the owner's decided order (underwater.md: 3 next, 4 with 6, then 5, then 7, then 8).

rejected.defect: M18 (part: the lineup shot shows no peak, reef, cliffs or cove)
rejected.reason: The sheet's lineup shot is designed to look along the lineup from 25 m behind the focus (waterSheet.ts:263), and the cove is scenery. Group 2 fixes the near field's smear.
The sun disc and its halo come from the sky photo and the tone mapper, not the water.
Its region (curl-close-rich-midday lip top, x 575-720) is the lip-top region listed under B1; the critic's text was cut off. Fixed with B1 in group 1.
The dithered parallelogram is B1's mask band at a front's end, and its zig-zag seam is B3's R-infinity at the band's edge. Fixed by groups 1 and 2.

ownerQuestions: Classic outside the swept barrel shows the same artefacts the critics flagged: cobalt dashes at grazing angles (waterOptics.ts:226-227), the 0.7 m Voronoi lace net (foamPattern.ts), a milky sun path, and a dawn horizon seam. Your rule keeps Classic byte-identical. Should we allow bug-only fixes there (the grazing fallback, and the lace's hard 0.04-cell edge), or keep Classic as it is?

Rich's gain 'through exposure' (decided 2026-09-29): raising the renderer's exposure 4x would also brighten the photographed sky 4x, and the Neutral tone mapper would clip it near white. Group 4 instead puts the gain on the whole water (body plus foam layer) and returns the sky's reflection to plain Fresnel (it had been halved by eye). Keep that, or move the gain into the renderer's exposure and accept or rebalance a brighter sky? The choice decides how warm the near water turns at sunset (M12).

The water in front of the curl sits a few decimetres over Padang's reef, because the forward rest holds the library's Basilisk trough. So the coral bed shows through as one flat khaki. A sourced bed would come from the Allen Coral Atlas's benthic layer (coral/algae, rock, rubble, sand) over the reef; its geomorphic layer is already used. That is a download needing your OK. Approve it?

The critics also want Padang's cove: limestone cliffs, jungle, and a sand beach with a shore break. That is scenery, outside water physics. Give it to another session, or leave the land plane, now lit in Rich, for this round?
triage r1.consultRow: | 2026-10-03 | Look critics, round 1 (three harsh critics on renders of the finished barrel: #104, #107 and #102 merged locally; Padang practice swell, curl and whitewater sheets) | Not yet: 10 blockers, 18 majors and 3 minors (the list cut off at m3). A dot grid where the curl meets the water (12.6 % of blocks at sunset); a flat teal ceiling in the tube; cobalt dashes at grazing angles; Voronoi foam and a white cell net on the near water; a pale glassy lip; khaki shallows and pea-green faces; an unlit beige land; a flat underwater; grey foam balls and orange spray discs; Rich flatter than Classic in 20 of 45 tiles. | Causes found in the code. The seam is a per-pixel noise dither with no temporal pass, between the water and a curl shaded without the water's crest light, normal and foam. The teal is the underwater fog: the camera test reads the solver's hump under the lip. The dashes are R∞ where perturbed normals face away. The white net is the foam lace, not glints (mint at every hour, and in Classic too). The khaki is the coral bed under the forward rest's few decimetres of water, with the sky's reflection halved. Five groups on disjoint files, face and tube first. (1) The curl: a blended band, the water's own shading where it rests, the crest light over the profile's chord, ripples and lace mapped along the face, no caustics under the lip, the throat opening toward the mouth, the lip's back light on the glow's path with a fraying white edge, and the undersides smoothed. Part B's follow-ups are assigned here; half floats stay unassigned, since no defect calls for them. (2) Rich optics: a normal guard, the bed path along the refracted ray, Padang's sourced colour (decided), specular anti-aliasing from curvature, a capillary octave, and Snell's window. (3) The camera test against the drawn barrel, the seabed lit in Rich, and underwater fog per spot. (4) Rich foam (decided): foam adds light, aged lace from a particle bake, and the sky at Fresnel. (5) The spray look (decided): foam balls lit as fresh foam, drops by optical depth, and the offshore veil on the relative wind. After (1) and (2) merge, the curl passes (2)'s body option (one line). Rejected: Classic-only artefacts (your rule), scenery (cliffs, jungle, cove), the sky photo's sun, the roller's volume and underwater items 3–8 (your order), and a reef texture (needs a download). Four questions to you. Outcome: building. |

build r1 g3 [sonnet].summary:
Three local commits on look-fix/r1-3, in <WORKTREES>/lookfix-r1-3 (not pushed). Group 3 is built, and the Padang numbers are measured on the water sheet.

Checks on the clean tree: `tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npm run build` succeeds. The barrel dirs, waterLooks, SweptBarrel and SweptBarrelMesh pass unchanged. The tests of every file I touched pass (23 files, 276 tests). `src/scene` as a whole also passes (60 files).

Fix 1, 337f685ef, a camera inside the drawn tube is in air (B9). The advisor's lines were right (main.ts:305, PhysicalMode.ts:735 and the three main.ts call sites). At the sheet's hold the curl-inside camera stood at 0.31 m while the solver's height was 0.81 m and the drawn surface under it 0.04 m.
- New `src/game/drawnWater.ts` counts the drawn loft's triangles above the point where the loft covers it, and falls back to the solver's height elsewhere. It reads only the loft's positions, indices and indexCount. I used a signed count (a winding number) rather than a parity, because two fronts' extensions can lie on the water as coincident sheets and a parity would cancel them. A test pins this.
- `PhysicalMode.pointBelowSurface` serves the game camera (fog, background, sound) and the sheet's renderView, once per drawing.
- Visual: the six curl-inside tiles no longer have the flat teal. Pixels within 3 of (54,126,131) in the top-right 40 % went from 100 % to 0 %, and the mouth now shows the sky and the land. Every other tile is pixel-identical.
- Cavity check: of 78 sample columns between the face and the lip's underside, the old test said under water in all 78 (all 8 I rendered were flagged). The new code flagged 0 of the 39 I rendered. All 13 cameras under the face stay under water.
- Cost: 0.26 ms for the largest loft the budget allows (78 700 triangles), under load.

Fix 2, 97b8cb02d, the Rich seabed is lit by the hour (B6, B10). It uses MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 1, taking the scene's sun and the photo sky's environment.
- Albedo is the spot's bed albedo under the water and the painted sand above the waterline [provisional], over a short wet band at the tide's waterline.
- `bedLight` in SpotSeabed.ts is the tested reference of the shader. The sun enters at (1 − F) and falls e^(−K d/μ_w). Its unscattered beam falls e^(−c d/μ_w) and carries the caustics. The sky enters at (1 − 0.066) and falls e^(−1.2 K d).
- Land mean colour at dawn, midday and sunset, Rich: (142,143,130), (209,198,161), (167,155,137). It was (213,196,151) at all three. The spread is 67/54/31 of 255.
- The bed at sunset is 44 % darker than at midday (the prototype measured 43 %).
- Classic is pixel-identical in every tile.
- Side effect: the painted bed's caustic window used to darken dry land with a dark rectangle in Rich. That is gone, because caustics now apply only where the bed is wet.
- Cost: inside the run-to-run noise.

Fix 3, 2353c9b71, the Rich underwater view fades per channel by the spot's own water (B10). It uses the prototype's form.
- New `src/scene/underwaterFog.ts` edits three's shared fog chunks, so it runs inside every material with no extra pass, before the tone mapping. Classic keeps three's FogExp2 path whole.
- The eye path is e^(−c d) per channel from `beamAttenuation`, with the 7 m floor scaling c while keeping the hue.

details.name: Commit 1 e5e18fb45 (fix 1), visual
details.value: Rich foam is a white additive-light layer: R = R_f + T_f^2 R_w / (1 - R_f R_w), with R_f = cover x {0.55 fresh, 0.25 lace, 0.10 streak} (Koepke 1984; the age proxy and the lace value are marked provisional). The 4x gain is now on the whole composite, in RICH_FOAM and RICH_FAR_FOAM (tank, far ocean, curl). Streaks lose their hand opacity. Fresh foam / water luminance: sunset shoulder 1.36 to 2.16, midday shoulder 3.25 to 4.87, beside 3.03 to 3.88, behind 3.25 to 3.67. Lace / water: beside 2.79 to 3.56, behind 2.43 to 3.00, sunset shoulder 1.22 to 1.43. Files: foamPattern.ts and test, richWaterGlsl.ts, streaks.ts, waterLooks.test.ts.

details.name: Commit 2 216c92300 (fix 2), visual
details.value: The Voronoi net and leopard print are replaced by a baked field of floating particles on a compressible random surface flow (compressibility 0.49, Fung 1992 and Larkin 2009). It is stored as Gaussian ranks in the churn map's free channels (RGBA8 1024^2, mipmapped, baked lazily on first GPU read so Classic never pays). Two flow phases and two ages are blended in Gaussian space before the threshold (Heitz and Neyret 2018) at about 12 m and 3 m, hex-tiled. The covered share is exactly the foam value, edges are as soft as the pixel footprint, a patch thins to one bubble layer at its edge, and streaks stay stretched along the flow. Validated against 1M forward particles (Spearman 0.92 at 1.5 turnovers, 0.85 at 3). GPU matches the CPU mirror to 0.0018 sigma over 960 points x 3 flow states. Files: foamBake.ts and test (new), churnTexture.ts and test, streaks.ts and test, richWaterGlsl.ts, waterLooks.test.ts.
